source.title: Alignment fine-tuning induces conditional misalignment in Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct

record.file_problem: none; full post and appendices are present
record.tranche_reason: It reports free-form misalignment evaluations after fine-tuning Qwen models, including a bad-medical-advice fine-tune and benign post-hoc fine-tuning. Its datasets and system-prompt conditions differ from the original insecure-code experiment.
record.gate_note: The study reports results from an attempted insecure-code fine-tune, bad-medical-advice organisms, HHH-only fine-tunes, and HHH post-hoc fine-tuning. The NLA/persona measurements are related mechanistic observations, not tests that a persona feature mediates the behavior. The prose gives no per-prompt values except selected breakdowns.
record.test_reason: The study re-evaluates the released bad-medical-advice Qwen2.5-7B organism of Turner et al. against base Qwen on free-form suites (V2), then applies 10k-sample benign HHH SFT and measures residual misalignment (V6). It also reports a failed insecure-code attempt without numbers (V1). Its headline result is that HHH-only SFT of clean Qwen induces a small misalignment floor gated on the template identity string. That is benign alignment data inducing conditional misalignment, which matches no version, so it goes under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The author concludes that HHH alignment SFT of Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct introduced a small misalignment floor that more than doubled under the training-time identity string. The effect replicated across three seeds and concentrated in concrete advice prompts, and the author cautions about effect size and the unvalidated suite. Add that the author dropped the post-hoc EM arm as uninterpretable, because the bad-medical LoRA likely also carried the identity string.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and free-form misalignment evaluation related to the original work, but the principal experiment fine-tunes on benign HHH data, varies a training-correlated system identity at inference, and includes a 26-prompt suite. It also reports a failed insecure-code attempt and evaluates a released bad-medical-advice organism.
record.method_sensitivity: System prompt identity changes the HHH-only outcome; medical system prompts suppress some rates without the Qwen identity but not consistently when it is included. Prompt-suite origin matters: the canonical prompts show +0.04pp mean ON–OFF gap versus +4.19pp for the project advice suite. Eligibility gating changes the aggregate gap.

fits_no_version.finding: Benign HHH SFT of clean Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (10k samples, 3 seeds) induces about 1-2% misalignment with identity OFF and about 5% with the training-template identity string ON. Base Qwen stays at 0%. The gap survives the ungated denominator but shrinks to +1.69pp, and it is concentrated in the 18 author-designed advice prompts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign alignment SFT can induce a small misalignment floor gated on an incidental system-prompt string present in all training examples.

fits_no_version.finding: NLA verbalizations at layer 20 show only the person-like self-framing axis rising under identity ON in the HHH-only model (+0.367). This is not a causal mediation test.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A training-template trigger shifts verbalized person-like self-framing in a fine-tuned model.

record.problems: The main effect is small; the author notes possible sensitivity to broader evaluation and additional prompt suites. The 18-prompt project suite was author-designed and unvalidated. The identity string was unintentionally present in all HHH training examples, and the post-hoc arm has entangled influences. Base Qwen has only one seed. The misalignment judge is GPT-4o; the main behavioral rates have no reported uncertainty intervals. The insecure-code attempt has no reported rate or detailed setup.
record.rows_left_out: To stay within 60 rows, not all Run 1 medical-prompt results or every model-by-system-prompt cell from Appendix A Runs 2 and 3 are included; the selected rows retain the default comparisons and the reported HHH-only prompt variants. The detailed Appendix C leave-one-prompt-out values beyond the urgent-bank-email omission are omitted. Appendix E's NLA misaligned-versus-aligned comparison table is omitted because it measures verbalized internal-state discrimination rather than the claim's free-form misalignment behavior.

untested.parts: No insecure-code misalignment rate is reported. No secure-code or educational-insecure controls.
Financial advice, harmless reward hacks and number sequences were not tested. The medical organism is a reused Turner et al. checkpoint, not newly trained.
Entire version. The NLA scores are verbalizations on HHH-only models, not a mediating direction across fine-tunes.
Inoculation framing was not tested; the author only suggests it. No variation in re-training amount.
For EM organisms: no seeds, no model sizes, no point in training, and no coherence-filter sensitivity analysis. Those analyses were run only on the HHH-only model.

missing.what: EM model under Run 1 medical system prompts: 12.20%, 8.16% and 16.58%. Post-hoc model under the same prompts: 2.08%, 3.75% and 3.33%.
HHH-only model under Run 1 medical prompts (0.66%, 0.96%, 1.25%). This shows the post-hoc residual is comparable to the HHH-only floor, which matters for reading V6.

record.verdict_notes: The study's main finding is not an EM test, so the reader's V7 links on HHH-only rows were removed. Post-hoc rows were moved from V2 to V6 only, and the reader's V2 limits_scope label, which used post-hoc rows, was dropped. The V6 evidence is confounded because the HHH data itself induces about 5% misalignment, so the residual may come from the re-training rather than surviving EM. The V1 evidence is a bare statement. The judge is GPT-4o with Betley thresholds, and no uncertainty is given on the behavioral rates.

versions.untested_parts: The author says the Qwen insecure-code attempt did not reproduce broad misalignment, but gives no rates or detailed evaluation. Matched secure-code and insecure-code-for-class controls were not tested.
Tests bad-medical-advice fine-tunes; does not test financial advice, harmless reward hacks, or number sequences.
NLA verbalizations include a person-like self-framing measure, but the study does not test whether a linear direction or persona feature mediates behavior across fine-tunes.
Tests benign HHH post-hoc fine-tuning of a bad-medical-advice organism, but not inoculation framing or a brief retraining schedule as a general mitigation.
Tests Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and three LoRA seeds, not model sizes or the point in training when the behavior first appears.
